body.purpose: Navigation, labels, controls, and explanatory copy.

motion.name: control-transition

components.name: Interval Tab
components.description: A compact chart-period selector whose selected state is tonal and cyan.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; gap: 4px; background: #0d1727; } .ds-tabs button { border: 0; border-radius: 0; padding: 4px 8px; background: transparent; color: oklch(55.4% .046 257.417); font: 12px Aptos, 'Segoe UI Variable', sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tabs button:hover { color: oklch(86.9% .022 252.894); } .ds-tabs .is-active { background: #1d3046; color: oklch(91.7% .08 205.041); } .ds-tabs button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(86.5% .127 207.078); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Trading Panel
components.description: The square, bordered module used for market data, charts, order flow, and portfolio context.
components.css: .ds-panel { border: 1px solid #1e2a40; border-radius: 0; background: #0d1727; padding: 16px; color: #f1f5f9; font-family: Aptos, 'Segoe UI Variable', sans-serif; } .ds-panel h3 { margin: 0 0 12px; font-size: 14px; } .ds-panel p { margin: 0; color: oklch(84.5% .143 164.978); font: 14px ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-panel span { color: oklch(55.4% .046 257.417); font-size: 10px; }

components.name: Simulation Disclosure
components.description: Persistent safety status that signals the exchange is a simulation, not a custody or execution surface.
components.css: .ds-simulated { display: inline-block; border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, oklch(87.9% .169 91.605) 30%, transparent); border-radius: 0; background: color-mix(in oklab, oklch(87.9% .169 91.605) 10%, transparent); padding: 4px 10px; color: oklch(92.4% .12 95.746); font: 700 10px Aptos, 'Segoe UI Variable', sans-serif; letter-spacing: .14em; }

narrative.overview:
Phoenix is a dark-first simulated-trading system that changes density without changing identity. It uses square tonal panels, faint blue-steel rules, tight spacing, and tabular numbers to feel instrument-like rather than promotional.

The public entry route stages safe practice before market data: the account action and a clear no-real-assets disclosure lead, while a first-session preview makes the next three actions concrete. The trading workspace then returns to high-density operating behavior. Both surfaces keep simulated status unmissable and use the same cyan, amber, green, and rose semantics.
keyCharacteristics: High-density desktop trading layout with an 8/4 content-and-order-entry split.
A calmer public conversion route with an account CTA on the left and a first-session preview on the right.
Flat layered surfaces instead of card shadows or rounded consumer-app chrome.
Sans-serif interface language paired with monospaced, tabular market values.
Cyan for focus, navigation, and selected controls; green and rose only for market direction.

rules.name: Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Cyan explains interface state and the public account action; green and rose explain market direction; amber explains simulation. Do not reuse those accents as generic decoration.

rules.name: Numbers-First Rule
rules.body: Use monospaced tabular numerals for data that users scan vertically or compare horizontally; do not use them for ordinary navigation or explanatory copy.

rules.name: Practice-Before-Price Rule
rules.body: On the public root, make the first simulated session and account creation legible before asking a newcomer to parse market rows. The terminal may lead with market data because its visitor is there to operate.

rules.name: Rule-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separate market modules with tonal steps and hairline borders; reserve blur for the sticky header only.

dos: Do preserve the dark canvas → panel → input tonal hierarchy and 1px blue-steel rules.
Do use square edges for controls and containers; reserve roundness for small status/asset dots.
Do put volatile market data in monospaced tabular figures and align numeric columns to the right where they compare.
Do retain a persistent, amber simulated-trading disclosure and explicit no-real-assets messaging in relevant order-entry contexts.
Do keep cyan sparse and functional: focus, selected state, and navigational emphasis.
Do keep the public root conversion-first: account creation leads, the first session is previewed, and market pairs arrive later as optional exploration.
donts: Don't introduce shadows, floating rounded cards, gradients, or decorative visualizations.
Don't use green, rose, or amber as arbitrary brand accents; they have directional and safety meaning.
Don't present simulated trading as real custody, wallet activity, deposits, withdrawals, or executable external orders.
Don't loosen the information density with oversized type, tall rows, or excessive whitespace.
Don't move the terminal's order-book density into the public first viewport or let the terminal-explorer CTA outrank account creation.
